entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.inflow: The Inflow dock before sunrise, wet from a storm, with return cages under amber work lights.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.core_floor: The night-shift Core Floor, with an inspection bench, instrumented test racks, and a safely opened server chassis.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.trace: A Trace analysis bench lit by a task lamp, with instruments and a hand-drawn fault tree.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.gate: The Validation Gate audit area, with a traveler station and distinct hold and release tags.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.knowledge: The Knowledge Systems desk, where attributable Worklog histories appear on a restrained timeline display.
entries.text.qc01.asset.bg.client_review: A practical client-review room at dawn, with a physical lot summary prepared for discussion.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.ev.focused: Ev Shaw stands compactly focused in a charcoal floor jacket.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.ev.concerned: Ev Shaw listens with visible concern, withholding judgment.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.inez.amused: Inez Calder holds a dock scanner with a dry, knowing smile.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.inez.focused: Inez Calder holds a dock scanner, focused on the intake work ahead.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.malik.focused: Malik Okoye holds a coiled Rigline test cable with focused attention.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.malik.defensiv: Malik Okoye holds the Rigline test cable in a guarded stance.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.sora.focused: Sora Chen stands ready to question an assumption, one hand raised and a closed notebook at her side.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.sora.approving: Sora Chen offers restrained approval, one hand extended and a closed notebook at her side.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.hana.skeptical: Hana Park holds a traveler at the Validation Gate with a skeptical, exact expression.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.hana.relief: Hana Park stands with the traveler tablet and a quietly relieved expression.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.jonah.defensiv: Jonah Reed holds the closed Worklog tablet in a guarded, attentive stance.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.jonah.thoughtf: Jonah Reed pauses thoughtfully with a closed Worklog tablet.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.priya.concerne: Priya Nayar reviews the lot summary with practical concern.
entries.text.qc01.asset.character.priya.resolved: Priya Nayar holds the completed brief with a resolved, steady expression.
entries.text.qc01.asset.insert.repeat_serial: A player-safe serial-history summary links one returned unit to a prior case whose Verify note only said that the unit tested good.
entries.text.qc01.asset.insert.sift_gap: A source-coverage summary distinguishes recorded results, unpublished outputs, missing context, and recommendation confidence.
entries.text.qc01.asset.insert.final_queue: A three-Ticket incident board lists a missing boot device, intermittent storage-path errors, and reduced array redundancy without naming their causes.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift01.title: Booting the Wrong Device
entries.text.qc01.match.shift01.setup: First Look has opened one Repair Ticket for a server that consistently selects an unintended boot source. Public Symptoms and Candidates are available; the underlying fault, decisive diagnostic path, required response, and eventual outcome remain unknown.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift02.title: Two Amber Lights
entries.text.qc01.match.shift02.setup: The shift board holds two separate Repair Tickets for unavailable redundant power paths. The warning matches, but each unit keeps its own Candidates, Evidence, and causal truth.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift03.title: Same Symptom, Different Memory
entries.text.qc01.match.shift03.setup: Rigline has reproduced two separate memory complaints: intermittent workload crashes and missing expected capacity. Each Ticket requires its own Evidence and post-Repair Verify.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift04.title: Passes Cold
entries.text.qc01.match.shift04.setup: Rigline has reproduced two thermal complaints under sustained work. Telemetry and physical cooling-path observations are public context; the causes and correct responses remain unknown.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift05.title: No Offer
entries.text.qc01.match.shift05.setup: Two network Tickets cannot reach their expected destinations. One interface retains physical link and one does not; link state and address configuration remain separate questions.
entries.text.qc01.match.shift06.title: The Quiet Cascade
entries.text.qc01.match.shift06.setup: The final shift board holds three independent Tickets: a missing expected boot device, intermittent storage-path errors, and reduced array redundancy. No Ticket supplies another Ticket’s Evidence or Isolation.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.open.01: The dock door is halfway open when the heat left by the storm finds you.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.open.02: Six returned Civic Atlas servers wait in two cages. The public-infrastructure cooperative needs them back in service, and one serial already appears in Trinity Hub’s authorized history.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.open.03: Inflow meets every unit before the repair floor does. The case file gives me one history; the box gives me another. Even my scanner knows better than to call either one the diagnosis.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.open.04: Ev wants the Continuity Rotation to carry useful context across every handoff. Which history leads the first brief?
entries.text.qc01.ch01.choice.intake.prompt: Choose which public history should lead; both will remain in the handoff.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.choice.intake.package: Lead with the packaging, seals, and custody route.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.choice.intake.worklog: Lead with the prior official Worklog chronology.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.package.01: The seal is new. The dent is old. The return route changed twice before the cage reached us.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.package.02: None of that names a fault. It tells First Look which observations arrived with the unit and which may have joined it in transit.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.worklog.01: The Worklog says the prior case closed after a boot correction. Its Verify—the independent post-Repair check—was current for that case, but the note says only “unit tested good.”
entries.text.qc01.ch01.worklog.02: That closure is chronology, not present truth. Carry what changed and the conditions that supported it. Investigate the unit in front of you.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.converge.01: Good. Public context chooses the next question. It does not answer the Ticket.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.01: First Look, the intake and triage team, has opened one Ticket for a unit that selects the wrong boot source every time. The complaint repeats; the cause is still yours to establish.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.02: Use the public observations to form a working Hypothesis. Then choose Tests that can make the Evidence support, contradict, or separate the Candidates. Which result would change your mind?
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.success.01: Gate has two things it can audit: a current, independent Verify of the required state and a Worklog that names the supported change. This unit may leave review.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.success.02: You corrected a boot choice. You did not prove that every future boot problem has the same cause.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.abandon.01: This Ticket ended without a closure-valid path. Give Up archived that case and revealed its answer only inside the player’s private Match review.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift01.abandon.02: Carry the gap forward. Do not turn it into a guess about the next unit.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.01: The shift board now holds two separate Tickets with the same lost-redundancy warning. One icon can describe several physical states.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.02: Use the similarity to choose questions, not to transfer conclusions. Each unit needs its own Evidence, accepted Isolation, Repair, and Verify.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.success.01: Both Worklogs now separate arrival observation, supported Isolation, machine change, and the current Verify that Gate can audit.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.success.02: Same warning, different Repair. That is why the warning was never the diagnosis.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.abandon.01: At least one power Ticket remains outside documented closure, so its unanswered work stays visible instead of borrowing the other unit’s result.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.shift02.abandon.02: Gate can hold a bounded unknown for another shift. It cannot release a confident sentence that outruns the record.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.ack.package.01: Your Inflow provenance survived First Look, the repair floor, and Gate. Hana can separate arrival observations from facts created during service.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.ack.worklog.01: Your prior Worklog chronology survived the repair-floor and Gate handoffs. Hana can compare the new work without treating the old closure as current truth.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.gate.earned.01: Your closed Tickets settled enough Story Service Points for the rotation to loosen supervision and let you choose the next leading question.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.gate.earned.02: Autonomy does not mean fewer checks. It means knowing which check must stay independent.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.gate.support.01: The rotation continues with closer review. Fewer Story Service Points mean less causal work settled at closure. They do not measure the learner as a person.
entries.text.qc01.ch01.gate.support.02: We will narrow the next question together, and we will keep every gap visible.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.entry.01: By the second week, the Continuity Rotation has moved you from intake toward systems test, analysis, and repair. People have begun leaving handoff questions at your bench.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.entry.02: Rigline reproduces complaints under named test profiles. Trace compares Candidates and designs observations that can support an accountable Isolation.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.choice.mentor.prompt: Which useful question should lead this review?
entries.text.qc01.ch02.choice.mentor.reproduce: Under what condition does the failure reproduce?
entries.text.qc01.ch02.choice.mentor.discriminat: Which result would distinguish the Candidates?
entries.text.qc01.ch02.rigline.01: A fixture is the rig plus the setup that made the result. Lose the target and operating condition and you have a very well-labeled souvenir. Yes, I own a label maker; no, it cannot restore missing context.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.rigline.02: Condition first. Then the Evidence can tell us whether that condition matters.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.trace.01: Possible is cheap. I have filled enough agenda margins with possibilities. Choose the observation that would make one Candidate different from the others.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.trace.02: Negative is not empty. If the Test reached the named target under the named condition, it can close one branch of the tree. Detach either, and we no longer know which branch moved.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.converge.01: Reproduction and discrimination answer different questions. Rigline makes the event available; Trace asks which result would make it useful.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.01: Two memory cases are ready. One loses expected capacity; the other fails intermittently under workload.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.02: A shared subsystem does not flatten different Symptoms or Candidates. Support each Repair, then Verify the required state on its own Ticket.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.success.01: Both memory Tickets reached documented closure, and each current Verify answers its own requirement.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.success.02: One part family can fail in more than one way. Each Worklog now carries the condition, Evidence, and supported explanation its next reader needs.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.abandon.01: At least one memory case ended before a closure-valid path was established.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift03.abandon.02: Bounded is a result. It is not permission to copy the other Ticket’s explanation across the gap.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.01: Same shape on both records: short idle stays inside range; sustained processor load climbs past it. The rig reproduced that change. It has not named what caused it.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.02: The rise does not choose among airflow, contact, or a moving part. Ask Bench for work the Evidence supports, not work the atmosphere suggests.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.success.01: The two thermal records now separate what the load reproduced from what the diagnostics isolated.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.success.02: The current load Verify matters because the Worklog keeps its load and duration attached. A detached green badge tells Gate only that something, somewhere, passed.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.abandon.01: At least one thermal case remains unresolved or archived after Give Up; any private revealed answer stays with that archived Ticket.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.shift04.abandon.02: We can retain the reproduced condition and the work already performed without pretending it became a complete explanation.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.ack.reproduce.01: You led with reproducibility. Each Worklog now names fixture and operating condition, so the next reader can tell a pass from a question the rig never asked.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.ack.discriminate.01: You led with discrimination. Each Worklog names the Candidate an observation separated. More data is not automatically better data.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.debrief.01: The repeat-return pattern is not one repeating fault. The repeated habit is letting a local result travel farther than the fixture, target, and condition that gave it meaning.
entries.text.qc01.ch02.debrief.02: Next shift, Knowledge Systems will show what happens when thousands of Worklogs preserve conclusions more reliably than their conditions.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.entry.01: Knowledge Systems maintains the Worklog platform, test-result integrations, and searchable service histories. Here, every omitted source condition becomes visible at scale.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.entry.02: SIFT indexes authorized words, serials, outcomes, and dates, then recommends related records. It cannot reconstruct a field nobody kept or decide what an old result proves now. I moved here from Rigline to build a map, not an oracle.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.entry.03: A missing source field is not Evidence of a secret shared fault. It is a stop sign on how far the explanation may travel.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.choice.record.prompt: Choose how the next Worklog review should help its receiving technician.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.choice.record.negatives: Preserve negative results with their targets and conditions.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.choice.record.summary: Lead with a bounded summary, then expose the supporting chronology.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.preserve.01: A negative result closes only the branch it tested. I will keep source, target, condition, output, and time together instead of burying them under “no issue found.”
entries.text.qc01.ch03.preserve.02: Then a later technician can see what was actually excluded and what remains merely untested.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.summary.01: The receiving technician needs the supported conclusion before the event stream. I will state its scope, then link to the Evidence and chronology beneath it. Summary as map, not trapdoor.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.summary.02: Then brevity becomes a map, not a replacement for the record.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.converge.01: Either policy works only when the Worklog still separates observation, interpretation, machine change, current Verify, and the person who recorded each step.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.01: Two network Tickets say only that an expected destination cannot be reached. One still has link. One does not.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.02: Keep link-state Evidence separate from address-configuration Evidence. Commit Isolation only when this Ticket’s current Evidence makes one public Candidate actionable.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.success.01: Both Tickets now have supported, separate explanations. The shared complaint helped organize the review; it did not authorize a shared Repair.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.success.02: And each Verify checks the state its own Repair was meant to restore.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.abandon.01: At least one network Ticket ended without documented closure. Its private archived answer cannot supply Evidence or Isolation to the surviving queue.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.shift05.abandon.02: Preserve the bounded gap. A missing closure is not a pattern waiting to be promoted.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.ack.negatives.01: Your negative results kept their source, target, and conditions. The next reader can distinguish a tested exclusion from an unasked question.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.ack.summary.01: Your bounded summary states what the record supports and links to the chronology. It saves the next team time without laundering uncertainty.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.debrief.01: SIFT surfaced a provenance gap by comparing authorized Worklogs. It did not diagnose a machine, restore an omitted result, or reveal hidden Ticket truth. That distinction is my responsibility too.
entries.text.qc01.ch03.debrief.02: The defensible pattern is procedural: independent ordinary faults become a quiet cascade when their explanations lose source context at handoffs.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.entry.01: At dawn, Client Programs prepares the supported outcomes, remaining risk, and release bounds that Civic Atlas can use. One question governs the brief: what can Trinity Hub responsibly put back in service?
entries.text.qc01.ch04.entry.02: I translate the floor’s authorized record into client decisions about scope, timing, and risk. I need a useful account, not one cause stretched over unrelated machines.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.entry.03: Priya, choose the order. We can disagree about the opening; the same Evidence, verified outcomes, and unresolved bounds must survive it.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.choice.frame.prompt: Which truthful order should the client account use?
entries.text.qc01.ch04.choice.frame.outcomes: Lead with verified outcomes, then state their bounds.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.choice.frame.uncertainty: Lead with bounded uncertainty, then state verified outcomes.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.outcomes.01: I will open with units whose named required states were independently verified, then point to the Worklogs that preserve each causal path. Outcome first; boundary attached.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.outcomes.02: Then name exactly what those passes do not establish about other units or future conditions.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.uncertainty.01: I will open with the bound: the reviewed record supports no common technical root, and unresolved Tickets remain explicitly separate.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.uncertainty.02: Then give the client the verified outcomes they can act on today.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.converge.01: Good. The client can act on a service risk created by lost handoff context. We do not need to invent a supplier defect, field condition, or shared component failure to make that useful.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.converge.02: Three final Tickets are ready. Coordinate the shared queue, but keep each machine’s Evidence, Isolation, Repair, Verify, and Worklog independent.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.01: One unit lacks its expected boot device. One has intermittent storage-path errors. One reports reduced array redundancy.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.02: No case lends its Isolation to another. Close only the causal path supported inside each Ticket, then document the limit the next handoff must retain.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.success.01: The final queue reached documented closure: three independent Tickets, three supported faults, and a current Verify tied to each unit’s named required state.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.success.02: That is an account I can defend. The coordination lesson connects the records; it does not collapse their technical causes.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.abandon.01: At least one final Ticket ended outside a closure-valid path. Its private disclosed answer remains an archived outcome, not reusable Worklog Evidence.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.shift06.abandon.02: We can give the client a bounded account of completed work and open risk. We cannot call the whole queue verified.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.release.01: Defensible Release. At least 20 of 24 possible Story Service Points support a client-facing account of the reviewed work while preserving every stated boundary.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.release.02: No single dramatic culprit. You made twelve independent explanations survive Inflow, First Look, Rigline, Trace, Bench, Gate, Knowledge Systems, and Client Programs. That is less theatrical and more useful.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.release.outcomes.0: Your opening verified outcomes first; the following bounds kept those results from becoming promises about machines they never tested.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.release.uncertaint: Your opening bounded uncertainty first; the verified outcomes that followed gave the client a useful path forward without hiding the limits.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.bounded.01: Bounded Account. The client gets three clearly separated sets: closure-valid work, private archived outcomes, and operating conditions that remain unverified. Useful does not require pretending those sets are one.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.bounded.02: The review authorizes only what the record supports. The remaining queue stays visible for another shift instead of disappearing into confident prose.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.bounded.outcomes.0: You led with verified outcomes and marked where that set ended. The account remains useful because the exclusions are visible.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.bounded.uncertaint: You led with uncertainty and followed it with the outcomes the client can use. The account remains bounded without becoming vague.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.hold.01: Gate Hold — Continue Training. Fewer than 12 of 24 possible Story Service Points support release, so the queue stays under Trinity Hub review—without shame and without invented certainty.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.hold.02: This is a safe operational fallback. Worklogs preserve completed actions, archived outcomes stay bounded to their Tickets, and open gaps remain available for another shift.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.hold.outcomes.01: You led with outcomes, but the record cannot yet support release. The hold prevents a partial success from speaking for the whole queue.
entries.text.qc01.ch04.ending.hold.uncertainty.0: You led with uncertainty, and the final hold gives that boundary operational force. The next shift inherits an honest queue.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.role.01: You are a new First Look technician at Second Current’s Trinity Hub, trained to handle hardware safely but new to the depot’s handoffs. The Continuity Rotation will follow what each team needs from the next.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.inflow.01: Before First Look gets the machine, I marry five things to the traveler: serial, route, box condition, accessories, and the complaint. Miss one and the next team inherits a mystery we made.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.records.01: Traveler for where it went and what went with it. Worklog for who did what, what came back, and what we accepted. Different histories; later teams need both to hold.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.lifecycle.01: One unit, one Ticket. Which plausible Candidate are you willing to call the Hypothesis? Good. Now choose a Test that can separate it from the rest; activity is not Evidence by itself.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.lifecycle.02: Commit Isolation only when this Ticket’s Evidence makes a fault actionable. Repair changes the machine; Verify independently checks the required state; Documentation carries the path to Gate. Give Up archives the Ticket, and its private answer stays there.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.points.success.01: Story Service Points count only closure-settled Isolation and necessary Repair contributions. Tests, Verify, Documentation, and closure are still required. Essential is not the same as separately scored; please spare me “administratively optional.”
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.points.abandon.01: Story Service Points count only Isolation and necessary Repair contributions settled at closure. A gap earns no invented points. Keeping it visible is still responsible work.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.specialists.01: Bench changes physical or configured state. We owe Bench the Evidence that makes the work supportable; Bench owes Gate the exact change and what it could have disturbed. Skip either half and a vanished symptom becomes an incomplete explanation.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.repeaters.01: Define repeater before the word starts doing our thinking. Here it means a unit returned after release. We have one confirmed serial and a repeated handoff habit—not a repeated symptom, an electronics device, or one proven technical cause.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.sift.01: Normally the rig publishes source, target, condition, output, and time. Strip those fields and SIFT can still echo the conclusion—cleanly, unfortunately—but the next technician cannot reconstruct the question.
entries.text.qc01.v2.context.client.01: Civic Atlas will use this account to decide what returns to service, what stays under review, and which uncertainty follows the unit to its operators. Make it readable, yes. Do not make it smoother than Gate and the Worklogs permit.
